title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

sense.text:
“Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.” A fable is a lie, and it is called Jewish because it pertains to the Jews. Christ was a Jew, and there is a lie being told about him: that he was born on December 25th. That is a Jewish fable. Christmas is a Jewish fable.

Christmas goes back into slavery, and it goes back into paganism too. It turns you away from the truth and from serving God, and it has nothing to do with Christ. Stop listening to Santa Claus, aka Pope Nicholas, St. Nicholas. Christ was not born on December 25th.

“And she brought forth her firstborn son”: her firstborn, meaning she had many kids. The dumb Christians in the Catholic Church say Mary was a virgin who never had sex, but it says her firstborn son because she had many sons.

She “wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger”. Christ was not born in the manger. He was born under an apple tree, and after she gave birth to him there she took him to the manger, “because there was no room for them in the inn.” The inn is a hotel, and there was no room in the hotels because everybody had come up for the feast. It was the Passover.

A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the winter time the animals go in the barn to stay warm. Around tabernacles time, the ingathering, they bring in all the animals and the crops to prepare for the mean season. So Christ was born in the springtime.

“And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field”: the shepherds were out in the field with the flock, not in the barn for the winter. Christ was born in the springtime, not in December. Don’t give heed to the Jewish fable that turns you away from the truth.

precepts.why:
Read to kill the fable of December 25th. “I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.” That is where Mary had Christ: under an apple tree. That is what the prophecy says.

After she gave birth to him under the apple tree, she took him to the manger, because there was no place in the inn. So Christ was not born in the manger.

This shows why there was no room in the inn. “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread”, which is the Passover, “and in the feast of weeks”, which is Pentecost, “and in the feast of tabernacles.”

Three times a year all flesh had to go up to Jerusalem, so the inns were full because everybody came up at that time. Christ was born at the Passover. That is why there was no room in the inn.

sense.text: “There came wise men from the east to Jerusalem.” East of Jerusalem is Babylon and the lands of the different captivities. Those wise men were Israel, living in the lands east of Jerusalem.

“For we have seen his star in the east”: the star they saw was a chariot, a light, what they call UFOs today. It is not the celestial body you see in the night sky. Something on the earth guided them and stood over the house. A star in the heaven, a planet, can’t do that.

Herod enquired of them “what time the star appeared”, and sent them to search for the young child, “that I may come and worship him also.” But Herod did not really want to worship him.

“The star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.” The star was guiding them. It is not talking about a planet.

“And when they were come into the house”: the house, not a barn. The Christians show the wise men at a manger giving gifts, but Christ was in a house. Time had passed, and he was now “the young child”, walking around: a toddler around two years old, starting to form words. You Christians do not understand the Bible.

They “fell down, and worshipped him” and “presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.” Christ was taken care of. He was well off. He wasn’t poor and he wasn’t a bum. And it was not three wise men: three is the number of the gifts. It was a caravan of wise men who saw the star and had been following it for at least two years, coming to Jerusalem to seek the king.

Being warned of God in a dream, “they departed into their own country another way.” The angel of the Lord told Joseph, “take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt”, for “Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.” They were there until the death of Herod, “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.”

Herod “slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under”. Herod killed thousands of black babies. Herod was a white man, an Edomite that converted to being a Jew, and Rome set him up as king of Judea, over Israel. He was no different from the white people you see today in the land of Israel. You see how evil the white man is.

So when you watch the news today and see the synagogues of Satan killing all these babies over in Palestine, it might surprise some, but it doesn’t surprise us: that is in their nature. That is who they are.

“According to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men”: the wise men had seen the star about two years before, so Christ was around two years old, and Herod killed every child two years old and under.
“And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.”

“His parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover. And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast.” So when did Christ turn twelve years old? On the Passover. Christ was born on the Passover, and he died on the Passover.

precepts.why:
The exact day and month Christ was born. “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.” The fourteenth day at evening is the fifteenth day. That is when Christ was born: the fifteenth day of the first month. Christ was not born on no December 25th.

Stop giving heed to Jewish fables, because it is going to turn you away from the truth: every one of you celebrating Christmas, following St. Nicholas, following the Pope, following that lie.
“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.” Christ is our Passover. He was born on the Passover and he died on the Passover.

sense.text:
“And he shall speak great words against the most High”: this is the white man, Edom. He has called himself the people of God, called himself Christ and the people of Christ, taken God’s land, and said that God’s laws are done away with.

“And shall wear out the saints of the most High”: he wore us out in slavery. When something is worn out it doesn’t look the same and you don’t remember. That is how we forgot who we are.

“And think to change times and laws.” It is the same thing Antiochus did. Antiochus IV Epiphanes, a Syrian king, forced the Jews to worship Greek gods, and desecrated the temple at Jerusalem on the 25th of Kislev, around December. They set up Zeus, they set up swine flesh and Bacchus, and had us worship Greek gods. It was unlawful for us to keep the festival days. The same thing is Christmas. God has festival days, and Satan does too: we have the dedication and Satan has Christmas; we have the Passover and Satan has Easter. There is always a counter, good set against evil.

America did the same thing: you don’t have to keep God’s feast days no more, why are you keeping Passover, why are you keeping dedication, Christ did away with them. Instead celebrate Christmas, celebrate Easter: here are some new holidays. And the dumb Christians follow them. They take our customs, twist them, mix them with paganism and feed them back to us.

It says he shall think to change times and laws because he is not going to be able to. The Most High is a mastermind. He has sent his sons, his prophets, back on the earth, and we are going to teach the right times, the feast days and God’s laws.

precepts.why:
There is a reason it says times and laws. “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years.” The sun and the moon are set up for time. The moon is used for time, so we can tell when our festival days come in.

So to change times and laws is to change the feast days and the customs, the same thing Antiochus did and the same thing America did.

sense.text: “We have also a more sure word of prophecy”: Peter is speaking, the apostles. Everybody doesn’t have it. The apostles understood the prophecies and what took place in the past. “A light that shineth in a dark place”: that is us.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.” Know this before you start reading the Bible. There is no different interpretation of the Bible: it says the same thing from the beginning to the end. There is a right way to interpret it and a wrong way to break it down. No: well, I think it means this.

There are key principles. The foundation of being an Israelite is that you went into slavery for breaking God’s laws; Jesus Christ is a black man, and he is coming back to redeem you, and only you, from your sins and to save you from your enemies. You have to keep God’s laws: stop committing adultery, stop lying and stealing, stop being evil, stop following Babylon and Babylon’s lies, and come out from among her.

As time goes by the Most High is going to increase all of us with more understanding of the scriptures. Our understanding grows as we grow spiritually, so we understand the hope and why we are doing what we are doing. And those the Lord God has set up to teach, the apostles on the earth, are going to teach it the right way.

“For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man”: man didn’t sit down and make stuff up. “But holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” The Most High spoke through the prophets, our forefathers.

All the prophets say the same thing, but in different ways, some with more detail than others. Anytime you think you see something in the scriptures and the other prophets do not say the same thing, you have your own interpretation.

precepts.why:
“And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge”. Prophecy is a gift. Paul had the gift of prophecy and understood all mysteries.

That is why, when you read the book of Hebrews, we understand a lot of things in Genesis: because of the letters of Paul. Paul took it to another level and made it plain for us, and a lot of things in the law that we don’t fully understand, Paul understood.

“Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” It is given unto the apostles and certain men to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, first and foremost. God reveals it to them, they reveal it to the people, and the people understand it. It is not given to everyone.

That is why there is no arguing with anybody about what the scriptures mean. Correct them and keep it moving: if God did not open your eyes, you are not going to get it.

sense.text:
“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom”: that is all of us, and that is these scriptures. What is being touched on today is hidden wisdom: the kingdom of Adam. Did Adam have a kingdom? I thought he was running around butt naked. No, there is hidden wisdom.

“Which God ordained before the world unto our glory”: that hidden wisdom is also going into Christ. Who Christ was and who he is was hid from our people for all ages.
“Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” If they had known who he was, they would not have killed our king.

“The things which God hath prepared for them that love him”: “God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit.” To understand what God has prepared for you, God has to reveal it to you by his Spirit; he has to put his Holy Spirit in you. Even some of you here believe but don’t fully understand what God has prepared for us: it is on another level. Then you read the scripture and say, this is the holy city; I am going to live forever; if I die right now keeping the commandments, I don’t really die, I am going to be with Christ.

“For the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” When you read, the Spirit is showing you things. There are deep things of God, and some of them are being touched on today.

“The things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God.” For us to understand the things of God, God must send his Spirit into us and show it to us.

“That we might know the things that are freely given to us of God.” There are a lot of things the Lord has freely given us: the kingdom of heaven, which is immortality. I know we are living in Babylon, struggling to pay rent, some going through sicknesses. Just keep his commandments and do what’s right.

“Not in the words which man’s wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth”. We didn’t go to no theology school or seminary to learn how to teach. We teach from the Spirit of God that dwells in us, “comparing spiritual things with spiritual.”

“But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God”: the sinful man. You tell him we are going to live forever if we keep the commandments, that when we die we are going to be with Christ, that Adam wasn’t walking around butt naked, and “they are foolishness unto him”. What are you doing for the community, my brother? We need to deal with economics. He thinks carnally; everything for him is worldly. If you can’t show him a plan, it is not by faith.

“Neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” So why are you trying to force him to know it, arguing with him about the scriptures? Correct him and dust off your shoes. Even when we teach you the scriptures, unless the Spirit of God opens your eyes, you are not going to see it.
“But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.”

precepts.why:
“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” There are two types of people in this world: people that say they love Jesus, and people that do what Jesus said. Which one is justified? If you are not doing what he says and you say you love him, you are a liar.

“He shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”, and “the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. To learn the different levels of understanding in the scriptures, God has to send his Holy Spirit, the Comforter, and it teaches us all things. It starts with the apostles and the 144, and they teach the people.

“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”. Some of us in here are apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors, some teachers, and some brothers have more gifts than others.

Why did God give us these gifts? Not to exalt yourself: I’m the mighty deacon. “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry”. Whether your gift is to prophesy, to teach, or to be an evangelist, it is not for your own selfish reason. It is to make the brothers better, to make the people perfect, to help your people. The brothers traveling the world teaching the gospel are waking people up, and the teachers show you how to change your life through the law. All of it is the gifts the Holy Spirit gives us to perfect the saints.

“Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.” Paul says, I would rather you prophesy, because “he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.”

When you prophesy, you teach and edify the people, and you exhort the brothers to continue in the faith and have hope. That is how brothers develop hope and faith: when the prophets amongst us prophesy and go into the scriptures and show certain things. That feeling inside when you hear brothers teach that can prophesy, that revives you, is the exhortation. And it comforts us, because we are all tired of this world and this life; when we see what the Lord has prepared for us, it comforts us to continue in this work.

“That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height”. The breadth, meaning the width: it is going into what the Lord has prepared for those of us that love him. Once you fully understand that, it gives you hope, it exhorts you and comforts you to continue in this walk and not fall out and go back in the world.

Some have been with us for years and say, I can’t take it no more, it’s been five years and I ain’t got none, me so horny, and they go back into the world and let Satan overcome them. If you want to get married, go to the Lord first: pray, fast, and say, Lord, send me a righteous husband, send me a righteous sister. But get yourself right first, or the Lord will say you ain’t ready. Sisters talk about wanting an Abraham but are not like Sarah, more like Rachel, the pretty face and the big booty, worshipping idols; Abraham is not going to deal with a loudmouth stubborn woman. And brothers want a Sarah while still living with mama.

“And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.” “Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end.” The church is that world without end.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” We worry about many things.

“And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth”: for centuries people ran around talking that the earth is flat, and even negroes today talk about the earth being flat. “But the things that are in heaven who hath searched out? And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above?” God has to give wisdom and send his Holy Spirit from above. That is how you understand the things in heaven and the counsel of the Lord.

“They that dwell upon the earth may understand nothing but that which is upon the earth: and he that dwelleth above the heavens may only understand the things that are above the height of the heavens.”

“Then answered I and said, I beseech thee, O Lord, let me have understanding”. Ezra wanted to know some deep stuff, the things above the heavens, so he asked the angel to give him understanding. And the angel revealed a lot of things in heaven to Ezra. To understand spiritual things, things on another level, the Lord has to reveal it to you.

sense.text: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”. This is the Lord speaking.
He led the people out of Egypt and brought Moses up to the mount, where he held him by him “a long season”: forty days and forty nights.

“And told him many wondrous things”: it wasn’t just the ten commandments. “And shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Moses saw these last days with Europe and America ruling.

And the secrets of the times are also the beginning. What does the word Genesis mean? The beginning. Many think the beginning starts with the earth. No: the beginning of creation did not start with the earth. It starts before the earth.

“These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” God told Moses to hide some stuff: the beginning of creation, the trees in the garden, Adam, and the water that runs through the garden. All these things are really talking about something else. Everything we read in Genesis is going into Adam’s kingdom, but it is hidden. Then the Lord sent other prophets to give us little bits and pieces.

precepts.why:
This is how Moses hid it. “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” Moses was a prophet, and God spoke by Moses in similitudes.

A similitude is like a metaphor: a likeness, a resemblance, a comparison. You make it sound like you are talking about a tree, but you don’t really mean a tree; it is something much heavier. When Genesis talks about the trees in the garden, he is comparing trees to human beings.

To understand these things, the Lord’s Spirit has to come into you. That is why the Lord told Moses to hide them: it is not meant for everybody to understand. But today some will understand these things.

“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The things that Moses hid are the secrets of wisdom, and they are double. You read a scripture and it is not just saying one thing; it is saying two things.

Many times we read a scripture and think we got it, then we read it again and the Most High makes us see something else on another level. Not that what we saw was wrong: there is just another level to it.

sense.text: “The firstborn of every creature”: Christ was the first thing created. He was created before the earth, before the heavens, before the angels. He is “the image of the invisible God”.

“For by him were all things created”: God created him and told him to create everything else, in the beginning, in Genesis. “That are in heaven”: the angels, the stars, the planets, the galaxies, and paradise too. Paradise is in heaven. “And that are in earth”.

“Visible and invisible”: there is a spiritual realm, things you cannot see that Christ created. And there are things on the earth no one has ever seen; Esau is still finding new species of fish in the ocean, and they have not seen leviathan as yet. Thrones, dominions, principalities and powers, visible and invisible.

“All things were created by him, and for him”: he is the Son, the heir. His Father told him to create all things, and all he created was by him and for him.

“And he is before all things.” Everything you could think of, Christ was before it.

Paul understood the depth and the width and the knowledge of God. The apostles and everyone following them back then understood a lot; the Spirit of God revealed the hidden mysteries to them. After the last apostles’ students died, the understanding died with them and all types of paganism came into the church. But God has sent his sons back on the earth again, and the proper understanding of these scriptures is coming back out.

precepts.why:
“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The secrets that Moses hid, God reveals unto his servants the prophets.

People question it: these guys say they are prophets. We are not going to say anything. You brothers and sisters online, judge for yourselves. We are going to show you some secrets, and you judge for yourself.

sense.text:
“In the beginning”: when did the beginning start? It started when Christ was created. It is the beginning of creation, and creation is not only the earth and the sky: it is the creation of everything. Many still read it today with an earthly, carnal mind.

“God created the heaven and the earth.” The top verse lets you know what God did in the beginning; then it explains how he did it, one thing after another.

“And the earth was without form and void”: the earth had no shape. There was nothing there; it was not yet created. “And darkness was upon the face of the deep.” When the scriptures talk about the deep, they are talking about the sea, the waters, and the Lord also calls space the deep. The waters in the heavens were just darkness; nothing was there. “And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters”: this lets you know that the deep is the waters.

What is mentioned first, before the earth was formed? Darkness: space covered in darkness. Darkness comes first because the Lord already had it set up that when we came down here we were going to be evil anyway. That is why it is the evening and the morning, why Cain was born first, why Edom was born first, why Ishmael came first, Esau before Jacob. Evil, darkness, goes first, then the light comes after. That is why Christ said the first shall be last and the last shall be first.

“Let there be light: and there was light.” This is not the sun or the moon; they were not created until the fourth day. Christ was the firstborn of all creation, so the first thing the Lord created was the light: Christ. That is literally what he was when he was created: a light.

The Lord told Moses, I want you to hide these things; don’t make it plain for everybody to understand. When you explain when my son was created, say the Lord said, Let there be light. That is why Christ is called the hidden wisdom, the hidden secrets.

This light is not light to light the earth, because the earth was not created as yet. When you read the Bible as a human being, you read it that way. That is why you cannot understand the things above unless the Lord sends his Spirit.

“And God divided the light from the darkness.” Even this is a similitude. Light is good and darkness is evil, so when the Lord divided light from darkness, he created good and evil. Spirits were created, angels were created, evil was created, Satan was created. And God said, you I am going to choose; you I am not going to choose, I am going to harden your heart.

That is the Lord choosing who is going to get the kingdom and who is not. We were in that light when it was formed, already in Christ, and then the Father said, that one, that one, that one; not that one, he goes over there on the left side.

“And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.” Was the earth created as yet? No. So this is a similitude: one thing used to explain something else. The light is called Day: Christ is called the day star; he is that Day. The darkness he called Night is evil: Satan that he created, and his angels, his minions.

“And the evening and the morning were the first day.” On the first day Christ was created, Satan was created, and the angels and his children were created. Angels is interchangeable: if we have an angelic body, we are angels. God always creates two and two, and everything he created he created perfect.

precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord spoke “from the beginning of the creation, even the first day”, saying “Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” The word that did that perfect work is Christ.

Read on and Ezra shows what was there before anything was made: “darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.” Nothing, a great void. “Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” That fair light out of God’s treasures is the light of Genesis 1:3, and it is worded that way because that light is what made everything else: it came forth so that God’s works could appear.

So “in the beginning” is not only the making of the earth and the sky. It is the beginning of all creation, and it begins with Christ, the first thing God created, the light called forth on the first day.

John opens the way Genesis does: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word that was with God is Christ. He was a God in the beginning, made in the image of his Father, creating angels, galaxies and planets. “The same was in the beginning with God”: two different persons, the Father and the Son.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Then: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness”. That is the same light God brought out of his treasures in 2 Esdras 6, the light of Genesis 1.

John the Baptist “came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”, with a capital L, and “He was not that Light.” Christ is “the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world”: the true light God created on the first day. When the Lord says, Let there be light, it is talking about Christ being created.

Christ says it himself: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” We read that Christ is the first thing created; we go to the first thing created and God says “Let there be light”; and here Christ says, I am that light. The scriptures line up, and still some say no.

That is why the light of Genesis 1:3 is not the light of the sun. The earth was “without form and void”, not yet made, and the sun and moon were not made until the fourth day. Read with a carnal mind, it sounds like daylight; read with the spirit, it is the Son.

When were the angels created? “In the beginning, when the earth was made, before the borders of the world stood, or ever the winds blew, Before it thundered and lightened, or ever the foundations of paradise were laid”. The foundations of paradise were laid: we are going to see some things today.

“Or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were gathered together”. The moveable powers and the multitude of angels were established in the beginning. Going back to Genesis, this is what else was created on the first day.

“Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness”. Darkness is evil and light is good. So when the Lord divided the light from the darkness, he created good and evil. Something is going on in Genesis 1 that Moses is letting us know.

“The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world. His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he hath separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.”

Adamant means refusing to be persuaded or to change one’s mind. He hardened Pharaoh’s heart so Pharaoh would not be persuaded to let us go. That is how God separates light from darkness: he hardens people’s minds. He will harden your heart so you will not believe these scriptures and will not follow.

So when Genesis says God separated light from darkness, spirits were created, angels were created, evil was created, Satan was created, and God said: you I am going to choose, my chosen people; you I am not going to choose, I am going to harden your heart.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. Predestined means an outcome determined in advance by divine will: you are going to get it no matter what. Foreordained, destined, predetermined.

Today no one knows whether or not they are predestined; when you make it to the kingdom, that is how you know. But when were we predestined? When God separated the light from the darkness. Shout out to the bishop who dropped this.

“Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness.” This lets us know when the children of light were created. In Genesis 1 it was not just the light created: the light created his children too. Christ said, I and the children are one. We were in that light when it was formed, already formed in Christ, just like Eve in Adam. The light he called Day, and we are the children of the day. Day and night were used to compare good and evil and the children of good and evil, all on the first day. Day and Night and Light are in capitals for emphasis: a specific day and a specific night, good and evil, right angels and wrong ones, right spirits and wrong spirits. The translators had the Spirit on them too.

“Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.” We should not be sleeping; we have to be aware of what time we are living in. “For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night.” Night was not made for working.

“But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. For God hath not appointed us to wrath”: because we are the children of the day, the children of the light.

Who is the day? “As unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light that shines in a dark place, because we are the children of the light. The day star that arises in our hearts is Christ. The Day, the day star, is that light which is Christ.

“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” The world was not yet made; those that now live are Israel. “For then every one obeyed”: before he created the earth, everyone that was with him obeyed. The man there is his children; the children of darkness were already reserved not to listen to him.

That is why the first day was not just Christ: angels were created, and we were there in our angelic body, our celestial body, the body we will have when Christ returns. We obeyed because we were not in this wicked fleshly body.

“But now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed, and by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves.” Created in the heavens, we were good; created in this earth, covered in this flesh, we are rebellious. Now the Lord says, you are in this flesh and you ain’t listening to nothing I say; I have to keep whooping you, worshipping idols and doing all types of evil.

There are levels and depth we have to get to, to have the hope and joy to go through what we will go through. It is the teacher’s job to make you see who you are, so you have that faith and hope and endure in this truth.

“Whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” When was your name written in the book of life? From the foundation of the world. That goes back to Genesis 1, when the Lord separated good from evil. That goes back into predestination.

Ain’t no heathen in that book. Gentile saviours are going to die with their Gentiles. They are not in the book of life; they are in the book of slavery, the register of chains.

John “fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things. Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book”. The angel says: I am a servant just like you, I am your brother, I am a prophet, and I keep the things written in this book.

So you understand a little more what the Lord means: when you were with me in the beginning, you all obeyed. We had our angelic body with him before the earth was created. That is why Christ says in Luke that those who understand the power of God will be equal unto the angels. This is no fairy tale book.

“If our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have a celestial body, eternal in the heavens. “For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”: this body is susceptible to sin, so we groan for our spiritual body.

“If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” Paul is explaining the nakedness Adam had in the beginning. It is a similitude: when Moses says Adam was naked, it doesn’t mean he was running around butt naked. It means Adam was in the flesh. Before that he had a spiritual body, and God took his spirit and put it in the flesh. That naked is the shame, the sinful nature. We groan “that mortality might be swallowed up of life”: we want our immortal body.

“Whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord”, Christ. “For we walk by faith, not by sight”, and are “willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.” When you die keeping the commandments, you are present with the Lord. That is for every brother and sister who is sick, whom the doctor says doesn’t have long to live, and for the brothers and sisters who have passed away: we understand where they are. Don’t be afraid; conquer that fear. If you did what’s right and dealt right with the saints, you are going to be with the Lord.

“By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” Satan was created on day one. He is that crooked serpent. After Christ was created, he created us, and Satan was also created.

“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” There was darkness and God created light. He created good and evil; he does not create good without evil. Even darkness was made perfect: Satan was made perfect. Satan did not rebel against God. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, and even right now he is doing what he is supposed to do. “One thing establisheth the good of another”.

“Against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” The rulers of the darkness of this world are Satan and his minions. That goes back to the darkness God called Night in Genesis 1.

“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is the dark one, Satan, the darkness. It tells you God made him that way: more subtil, a deceiver. He wasn’t right, but God made him that way. Satan knows there is one God and trembles; he does not rebel against God. God created him to do exactly what he does: to tempt.

sense.text:
“Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.” The waters are space. Space was already there; now he is forming a sky, layers of atmosphere, in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor circle, and vapor means water: a water sphere that circles the earth and protects it from the sun. There are layers of heaven for the earth, then space, then paradise, and levels there: as above, so below.

The firmament divided “the waters which were under the firmament”, the sea, “from the waters which were above the firmament”, space. And there are different waters above the firmament. The same way you have fresh water and salt water, there is a different level of water above. You drink that water there and you are good for eternity. Moses is writing in a similitude.

“And God called the firmament Heaven.” Remember the secrets of wisdom are double. We read it and say God created the sky and space and that’s it, but there is much more to it; the spirit of God has to open your eyes. This is the heaven being created, and it is also going into paradise being created. The firmament and paradise, which is called heaven, were created on the second day.

“Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear”: they were not gathered together yet; there was no shape or form down here. “And God called the dry land Earth”: this is the earth being created. The heavens were created, and now the earth. He gathered all the waters together and called them Seas, the oceans. This was done on the third day.

Then grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree. The earth was being created and taking form and shape: not just the earth, but trees, fruits and grass. “And the evening and the morning were the third day.” The earth was created on the third day.

precepts.why:
“Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.” All the host of them: the angels, Satan, everything was created.

The word heavens there is plural. When God created the heaven, the earth was not there yet. There was the heaven, the atmosphere that separates the waters above from the waters beneath; there was space, another level of heaven; and after space there is paradise, which is also called heaven. So when God made a firmament and called it Heaven, he is not just talking about the sky over the earth.

Paul explains it. A man “caught up to the third heaven”, “caught up into paradise”. Paul calls paradise the third heaven: you have the sky, you have space, and then you have where the Lord dwells, which is paradise.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude: he created the sky, and he also created paradise. Everybody is not supposed to understand that, which is why Moses wrote it so that you need the other prophets to understand him.

Paul went to paradise and “heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” Those words are also going into the name. They were up there praising the Lord, and it is not lawful for him to speak that name.

“Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning: Genesis. Which part of Genesis was paradise created? When he made the firmament and called it Heaven: not just the firmament down here, but paradise, the third heaven. Solomon built the temple after the resemblance of what is in the heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world”: that is Christ; he was there. “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what is pleasing unto God: wisdom has to come and show you.

The temple Solomon built after the resemblance in the heavens: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. It is not coincidence that the temple was built with three stories, three floors. It is the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. It speaks of a chamber here and a chamber there, and 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

Noah’s ark: “A window shalt thou make to the ark”, there is that window again like the temple, “and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” Noah’s ark had three levels too, the same as the temple. It was a floating temple.

“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. The stories he builds in the heaven are the three layers: the first, the second and the third. That is what Paul calls the third heaven.

And the Father is above all heavens, at the very top, infinite, in eternity: the holy of holies. That is why he is called the majesty on high, the highest. That is one of the few titles Christ does not have: the Most High, the highest, is his Father. They are not the same entity.

“And hath founded his troop in the earth”: the troop is us.

“And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leddest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

Paradise was created in the beginning, but before the earth came forth. So paradise was created on the second day, and the earth on the third day.

When you think first, second, third day, your earthly mind thinks 24 hours. When Christ was created, was the earth created? Did earth time exist? Were the sun and moon created? Did 24 hours exist? No.

“That one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” Our time and God’s time are not the same. Don’t sit down and say God created the earth in 7,000 years. In that realm, time is different. The easiest way for Moses to explain it to our human minds was first day, second day, third day, but they are not earth days. Better to say: the first thing God did, the second thing, the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and then the seventh. What came out of his mouth, he said do this, and Christ did it.

And it had to be given in human terms, because the Sabbath account is based on the creation account. If it were given to us in God’s format we would be lost and confused, thinking every Sabbath is every thousand years, and we would be dead and gone before we rested. Moses wrote it in such a way that God’s Spirit has to come on you to reveal these things: even if we teach it to you, unless the Spirit of God is in you, you are not going to understand it.

“For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place”. The high and lofty One is the Father, and he inhabits eternity. Christ was with him in the beginning in eternity: the Word was with God. The Lord tells him what to do and he does it; he saw his Father create, and whatever he does he learned from his Father.

The high and holy place is above the heavens, above paradise: the holy of holies, the fourth floor, restricted access. No man has been up there.

“The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravel stone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.” When you go into eternity, a thousand years is like nothing. That is how it is where the Father is: the Ancient of days, the days of eternity. He sees the future back and forth, like something he already lived, because he lives in eternity.

“Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?” No one. Who can count God’s days? He is infinite, the Ancient of days. He existed outside the realm of time, before time.

So paradise was created before the earth came forward, which is the second day. When God created the heaven, he created not just the heaven that separates the waters above from the waters beneath, but paradise.

“He searcheth the deep, and the treasures thereof; he hath measured the sea, and what it containeth. He hath shut the sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word hath he hanged the earth upon the waters.” The water is space. When you look at the earth, all around it is space; it is like an ornament the Lord just hung there. Astronauts train in the water because that is where they are going: spend too much time in space and your bones get brittle, the same as going too deep under water.

“He spreadeth out the heavens like a vault; upon the waters hath he founded it.” A vault is an arch: it goes around, round, not flat. Upon the waters, space, he founded it: it is established there and it don’t move. The sun moves; the earth is founded. The devil says the opposite.

You are going to believe the man that says the earth is flat? A Colombian billionaire offered his $3 billion company to anyone who can prove the earth is flat. All you flat-earthers could be billionaires. Even the white man makes fun of you.

Job calls the water something else. “He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.” When you see the earth in space, it is on nothing: you can’t see the water, but it is there surrounding it. The nothing is the water. And the earth does not move or float off one way or the other. That is God showing his power.

There are waters below the firmament and waters above it. “If I should ask thee how great dwellings are in the midst of the sea”: how deep is it? That is why the Bible calls it the deep. “Or how many springs are in the beginning of the deep”: there are literal springs in the ocean. “Or how many springs are above the firmament”: above the firmament, in space and beyond, there are different springs. It is not just space; there are different waters up there.

“Or which are the outgoings of paradise”: the outgoings are the exits. Where does paradise begin? How do you get there, and how do you get out? These are the springs and the waters above the heavens.

“Whither I go, ye cannot come.” “Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world.” There are waters below and waters above, the same way Christ says, I am from above. Above is heaven. Where Christ is from, above, there are waters up there too.

“A pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.” That river issuing from the throne of God is the waters above. “On either side of the river, was there the tree of life”.

What we read here is a future prophecy that is going to happen, but this also happened in the time of Adam: the tree of life.

“No heart can think upon these things worthily: and who is able to conceive his ways? It is a tempest which no man can see: for the most part of his works are hid.” Most of God’s works are hid. The things he wants us to understand he reveals to us, and some things we are not going to fully understand until we are in the kingdom.

sense.text: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night”. Now the Lord is creating day and night on the earth. Day and night on the earth is different from the day and night of the first day of creation, which is good and evil; Moses uses it as a similitude. God created the sun and the moon: the light created on the first day was not the sun nor the moon. “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.”
“And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.” The stars, the sun and the moon were created on the fourth day. Time on earth was created on the fourth day.

“Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth”: the birds came forth from the waters. Then the whales and every living creature, and on the sixth day the beasts, the cattle and every creeping thing.

“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”. Adam was created to be immortal: that is how Adam was before he sinned. To be created in God’s image is not just how we look; it is also going into his power and his divinity. God created Adam to be just like him: immortal and righteous.

“And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”: that is the kingdom of Adam, in so many words. Let him have dominion.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him”. Only Adam was created in God’s image; everyone else was not. The sons of God are the ones created in Adam’s image, because Adam was created in God’s image.

“Male and female created he them.” Chapter one is the abbreviation, and Genesis 2 explains it, the same way Genesis 10 mentions Babel and Genesis 11 explains why it is called Babel.

And between verse 26 and verse 27 a lot of time went by. Moses said something heavy here because Moses saw something heavy. There is a big gap there, after Adam had dominion.

“And God blessed them”: he blessed Adam and Eve. “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it”. To replenish something is to fill it up again. And to subdue it: I thought he had dominion over it before. Why is God telling him now to subdue the earth? Those two things are opened up at the end, after the fall of Adam. When the bishop first brought this out, it took a couple of hours to get it.

“I have given you every herb bearing seed”, “and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.” That is what we were eating: fruits. “And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.”

precepts.why:
Genesis 2 explains how God created man in his image. “And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”. The dust of the ground is brown: Adam was a black man. And he wasn’t walking around butt naked.

“And breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: he gave him life. He put that spirit inside him, which is his son from the beginning. “And man became a living soul.” That is how Adam was created.

“But for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs”, “and the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.”

This is Eve being created. Eve was created from Adam, and Adam was created from the ground. This is the male and female of Genesis 1:27.

What does it mean, Let us make man in our image? “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” Adam was created to be immortal, in the image of God after his own eternity. Adam had power. That is how he was when he was created, before he sinned.

“Even so perisheth man also, which is formed with thy hands, and is called thine own image, because thou art like unto him”. Adam was just like his Father: like when somebody says, you are just like your father, you are the image of your father. It is the same with us: we are supposed to be in the image of Christ, and he is in the image of the Father.

“For whose sake thou hast made all things”: all things were created for Adam, and for the sons of Adam, which is us.

sense.text: “Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.”

“And he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.” People say: was God tired? That don’t make no sense. Moses is speaking in a similitude. God resting on the seventh day is talking about a place: paradise. A lot of people celebrating the seventh-day Sabbath don’t understand what it represents, or what Christ meant when he said he is Lord of the Sabbath, or that the Sabbath was made for man and not man for the Sabbath.

precepts.why:
“Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.” The word preached did not profit them, “not being mixed with faith in them that heard it”, because they didn’t believe. “For we which have believed do enter into rest”, “although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.”

“For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works. And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.” He was speaking of a place. When it says God rested on the seventh day, it is talking about him entering into his rest: paradise.

“There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works”. The works is us laboring on this earth to bring forth the kingdom of heaven.

It says he entered into his rest, and it is talking about a place. “And thou leddest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was planted before the earth: paradise on the second day, the earth on the third.

The Lord led Adam into paradise: that is entering into his rest. Not, I’m tired, let me get some sleep. Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth. He and his wife were the only flesh that could, until he committed sin and they said, you can’t be here. Flesh and blood can’t be up there because flesh and blood has that sinful nature. Adam is the only person who was able to go there in the flesh.

“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” We are praying to the Lord that his kingdom come on earth as it is in heaven. When Adam had dominion on the earth, it was on a much higher level than people think. How Adam was on the earth is basically how we are going to be in the future, the only difference being that we won’t be in the flesh, naked.

“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” When you go into the land and keep the commandments, your days are going to be as the days of heaven upon the earth. Moses saw Adam’s kingdom: he saw the old world, Adam ruling, the kingdom, the tree of life, and understood what it is all about. So he says your days are going to be just like that, the kingdom of heaven upon the earth, if you keep God’s commandments.

The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam was ruling.

“And the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.” The bride withdrawn from the earth is the holy city Jerusalem: the access to the spirit realm withdrew itself from the earth. For it to be withdrawn from the earth, it had to be on the earth, and it was, during the time of Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked; he was going back and forth to a spiritual realm.

How is that city described? Twelve gates, the twelve tribes of Israel, no heathens. Adam went through the Judah gate. Those gates were around, so those tribes were around back then. The twelve tribes in the beginning were called the sons of God: the tribes had not come forward on the earth as yet, so Moses says the sons of God. The Lord said, hide these things; they cannot know that they were around before.

“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven”. It withdrew itself, and now it is coming back. The names are written on the gates, and that city was prepared from the foundation of the world: the city was already built from the beginning.

sense.text: “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”.

“The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water: And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.”

“If this city now were given unto a man for an inheritance”: that city is the kingdom of heaven, and that is our inheritance. “If he never shall pass the danger set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?” The dangers set before it are us fighting and overcoming our lust, and teaching the word of God in persecution.

“Even so also is Israel’s portion.” Israel’s portion, not the whole world’s. “Because for their sakes I made the world”: for Israel’s sake the world was created. “And when Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” The decree is that we have to come on this earth and labor, full of sorrows, and the way is narrow, fire on one side and water on the other. That is after Adam sinned.

“Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail: they are but few and evil”: you live seventy or eighty years at most. “And very painful”: everything we go through on this earth is very painful, captivity after captivity.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world is the old world: the kingdom of Adam. When Adam sinned, the decree was set that we have to come on this earth and catch hell. But before that, the entrance was wide and sure. When the Lord created you, you were going to get the kingdom. All of us were there in the elder world ruling with Adam: all twelve tribes, every Israelite man. When Adam sinned, all that changed.

“If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.” The Lord wants us to labor now. If we don’t, we will not receive what is laid up: the city, the kingdom of heaven. In the old world it was wide and sure and we all got the kingdom; now we have to work for it. An inheritance is usually just given, but God says, I am not just giving it to you; you have to work for your inheritance.

“Why disquietest thou thyself, seeing thou art but a corruptible man?” Stop worrying yourself. “Why hast thou not considered in thy mind this thing that is to come”: consider the thing that is to come, which is the kingdom.

precepts.why: The old world was wide and sure: we all were there. “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning”. As at the first is the elder world, when Adam was ruling. When we were set up as judges back then, we were not in the flesh; we were immortal. There were judges set up when Adam was ruling: the twelve tribes of Israel were set up with him, ruling with him. And the beginning is Genesis.

“Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we. Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning.” The tribes of Jacob were with the Lord in the beginning, in Genesis. In Genesis 2 the sons of God were there; when Adam fell the sons of God were there. There was a government set up, rulership, a kingdom, with Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked. You had the gates of Levi, of Benjamin, of Manasseh: all twelve tribes in the beginning with the Lord, in their spiritual bodies.

People ask what tribe Abraham was from, what tribe Isaac was from. The twelve tribes were always there. When you go back to Genesis 6, the sons of God are the twelve tribes; Moses just says the sons of God, the same way we say today that we are the sons of God. Once you are the sons of God, you are one of the tribes of Israel.

“Upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.” We are named God’s firstborn because he created us first, before the world began. “O be merciful unto Jerusalem, thy holy city, the place of thy rest”: the place of God’s rest is Jerusalem, the holy city.

“Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.” The twelve tribes of Israel were always with the Lord from the beginning. And in these last days God has raised up the prophets that have been in his name, the prophets of old. The prophets are back: Enoch, Noah, Methuselah, Abraham back in the tribes of Israel.

“For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful”: healthy. We were living forever. “And there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth”.

There was no kingdom of death. The kingdom of death was established after Adam fell, when Satan and his children started ruling this earth. The kingdom of death is the white man and Satan ruling the earth. Before that was the kingdom of Adam, the kingdom of heaven. That is why Moses says your days are going to be as the days of heaven: he saw Adam rule.

“for righteousness is immortal” That is why man was created in the image of God after his eternity: keep God’s laws and you are going to be immortal and live forever. “But ungodly men with their works and words called it to them”, “and made a covenant with it”. A lot of our people have made a covenant with death. When Adam fell, Satan was given power over this earth, and a lot of our people are worshipping Satan; we are living in the kingdom of death. That is why the last thing Christ has to conquer is death: there will be no more death, period.

sense.text: “And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.”

“And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” That garden eastward in Eden is not talking about an earthly garden. It is the heavenly garden: paradise. After he formed the man, he put him there.

Adam’s kingdom was ruling the heaven and the earth. Adam had rulership over the heaven and the earth. You are telling me this man could go to paradise where the Lord is, and he ain’t got no clothes? You Christians are crazy and stupid.

“Every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food” is a similitude: it is talking about Adam’s sons in the heavens, the righteous. “The tree of life also in the midst of the garden”: the tree of life is up there; the twelve apostles were up there, the 144 were there, all twelve tribes were there. “And the tree of knowledge of good and evil”: Satan was there. The tree of the knowledge of good and evil is Satan.

That is the tree you are referencing right now in your house. Any tree you are robing and worshipping is the tree you are referencing. Babylon referenced it, and now you do it with Santa Claus: Saint Nicholas Claus, Satan Claus.

“And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.” The Most High did two things here. It is a similitude: it is talking about the waters above, which he separated from the waters below. And it is also going into rulership: there are trees by those rivers, and it is talking about Adam’s governance. It is talking about the heavens, and that also came down on the earth.

Pison, which compasseth Havilah, “where there is gold”; Gihon, which compasseth Ethiopia; Hiddekel, “which goeth toward the east of Assyria”; and Euphrates. What is going forth through all those rivers is the wisdom of God, wisdom and understanding, going into Adam’s sons ruling the earth in righteousness. It starts in the heavens and it is on the earth too. God had leaders, men set up throughout those regions, enforcing his laws. His trees were there, setting up his laws: on earth as it is in heaven.

“And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” To dress it and to keep it means to rule. Adam was ruling the heaven and the earth, and we don’t know how long it lasted. From the time Adam was ruling to Genesis 3, when Satan came and tempted him, could have been hundreds or thousands of years.

Adam was 930 years old when he died. When did his days start to be numbered? After he sinned. Before he sinned he was immortal. So how long did Adam live before his days were numbered? That is the kingdom of Adam. Before Adam was kicked out of the garden and could no longer go back into paradise, he lived a long time.

And Adam had children on the earth and children in the heavens. His children in the heavens were his firstborn, the twelve tribes; on the earth he had children of men that he made with his wife. A lot of time passes in Genesis 2: Adam is ruling the heaven and the earth. It sounds like a fairy tale to some, but it is talking about rulership of the earth and the heavens.

precepts.why:
“And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leddest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

It is saying the same thing as Genesis 2:8. The garden God planted eastward in Eden, where he put the man he had formed, is paradise.

What is every tree that is pleasant to the sight? “That they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”. The trees of righteousness are Israel: that is us in paradise, in our heavenly bodies.

“Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly”, but “his delight is in the law of the Lord”. “And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”.

God and the prophets work hand in hand. God has Moses write something hard, has the other prophets come and explain what he is talking about, then lets his prophets come back and decipher it. The trees pleasant to the sight are a similitude for Adam’s sons in the heavens, and the good for food is the righteous.

“He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.” Those are the four rivers we read about in Genesis. That water is wisdom and understanding. The waters up there are different: Lord, let me get just a little touch of that water there.

“The first man knew her not perfectly”: the first man is Adam, and he did not know her perfectly because Adam sinned. “No more shall the last find her out”: wisdom is infinite. “For her thoughts are more than the sea”, the sea of glass in Revelation, that clear crystal water, “and her counsels profounder than the great deep”: the great deep is space.

“I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. I said, I will water my best garden”: the best garden is paradise. That is the wisdom coming to the children of God. “And, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea. I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning”.

“And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire”. The brook became a river and the river became a sea: the sea of glass is going into that wisdom, that clear water, the water in heaven. The waters above that the Lord divided from the waters below are the wisdom above in paradise.

“And them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass”. We overcame the white man and his lies, and we are standing on the sea of glass, the clear water.

“In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” The tree of life by the river, as in the garden.

“Behold, a door was opened in heaven”: the heaven is paradise. John saw a door open going to paradise. “Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter.” John went into paradise, and that is where those things were shown to him.

“And before the throne there was a sea of glass”. We try to fathom it, but the sea of glass is wisdom coming from the throne of God. Esau put it in Marvel and called it the Bifrost: a bridge. It is a bridge leading from the Father down to paradise, down to the earth.
“Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light. Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.” The waters above the heavens.

“The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” Those that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality, the tree of life in the garden.

“A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.” Any and everybody can’t go there. “Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits”.

“A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.” Christ says he is the living water. Above the heavens is something called living waters. Christ told the woman, if you knew who asks of you to drink, I would give you living water, and she said she wanted some of that living water. That is the waters above the heavens, one of the springs up there.

“Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.” That goes back to Genesis: the Lord made every tree to grow in the garden that was good for food.

Balaam “saw the vision of the Almighty”. “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.” The tabernacles are not houses: they are our bodies, us being that tree by the river. Balaam saw us in our majesty when Christ returns, like cedar trees beside the living waters.

“He shall pour the water out of his buckets”: the waters are going to be poured out from on high. “And his seed shall be in many waters”: we are going to be swimming in those living waters, the waters above the firmament. “And his king shall be higher than Agag”: his king is Christ. “And his kingdom shall be exalted”: that is the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

These things are taught to encourage you, to build your hope up and exhort you: things that have been hid for thousands of years.

“That living waters shall go out from Jerusalem”: that is wisdom going forth from Jerusalem. The wisdom coming down from the Father goes to Christ, to the leaders, and the leaders issue that wisdom throughout the earth. So when it talks about the garden it is talking about the heavens, but on the earth also God’s glory and wisdom go out. That is why it mentions the Tigris and those rivers.

“Half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be”: all year round. The living waters going forth are the Lord setting up order and structure on the earth, the wisdom of God being taught on the earth.

“And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”. Christ is going to be king over all the earth: Adam is going to be back king over all the earth.

sense.text:
What scripture proves that Adam had kids before he fell? It is right there in front of our eyes. “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” She was a mother: she was bringing forth kids. This is before she fell, before Adam was kicked out. Eve was the mother of all the children living on the earth before they fell.

And Eve was a black woman, and she was beautiful. That was Adam and Eve in their kingdom. It wasn’t no people walking around butt naked.

precepts.why:
“And thou leddest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward. And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed”. Adam was given commandments and transgressed them.

“And immediately thou appointedst death in him”: when Adam broke God’s laws he was cast out of paradise, and now he had to die. Immortality was taken away from him. “And in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds”: everybody living at that time. There were nations, tribes, people and kindreds around, so Adam was probably on the earth for hundreds or thousands of years, and Eve was the mother of them all.

“And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures”. Adam was lord on the earth, ruling the earth and the heavens, and his creatures include the angels: Adam was over them. “Of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.”

But this verse is talking about after the flood, from Noah. Before Noah, before Adam fell, there were people.

“Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind”. That is not specific; it is broad, because all mankind came from Adam and Eve through their three sons.

Adam and Eve had kids before Adam fell: kids in paradise and kids on the earth. That is how Cain was able to find his wife. First came Cain and Abel after they fell, Cain killed Abel, and then Cain went and got a wife. Where did that wife come from? There were a lot of people living on the earth, tribes and nations, and Adam was governing them all. Those on the earth were not like those in the heaven. How the kingdom is going to be in the future is how it was then: we will have angelic bodies governing and ruling the nations, and it was like that with Adam. We were with him in the beginning, the twelve tribes, ruling the heavens and the earth with him.

sense.text: “Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude; Whom art thou like in thy greatness?” What follows, the Lord is using Adam’s kingdom in Genesis to give us a one-up: to explain what was going on when Adam was ruling. The Lord speaks to the prophets in similitudes, saying one thing but meaning something else. He is about to compare Adam’s kingdom to the Egyptian kingdom.
“Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.”

“The waters made him great”. Who is he comparing this to? Adam. What made Adam great was the waters that came from the Father. When God cut Adam off from that, you see what took place. “The deep set him up on high with her rivers running round about his plants”: his plants are all Adam’s children. The waters were flowing from him through all of them. That is how it was in Adam’s kingdom.

“His boughs were multiplied, and his branches became long because of the multitude of waters”. His branches and boughs are Israel, the sons of God, all of us who were drinking the water. Everybody wasn’t getting that water like us. “His height was exalted above all the trees of the field”.

“All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs”: the angels were under Adam. “And under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young”: the beasts of the field were under him too, Satan among them. “And under his shadow dwelt all great nations”: this is the earth. All the great nations on the earth were under him. Adam ruled in the heaven and the earth.

“Thus was he fair in his greatness”: Adam was great on the earth. He had access to the tree of life; he was around the angels; all of us around him had angelic bodies, and everybody was subject unto him, the kingdom of Adam. “For his root was by great waters”: those great waters are the living waters in the heavens.

“The fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches”. He is comparing trees to trees: the children Adam had on earth before the fall, who were not created in his image, against the children he had in heaven, in paradise. His boughs and branches are his firstborn; they were heavenly. The other trees are the different nations and people on the earth, and they were not like Adam’s children. Both realms were being ruled; Adam wasn’t ruling the earth alone. There was a portal open, Jacob’s ladder, with the sons of God ascending and descending.

It is the same when Christ returns: we will be changed in the twinkling of an eye, and the nations are not going to be like us.

“So that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” Who envied Adam? The children that were not created in his image, born before he fell. They envied him, and they envied us: the twelve tribes with him, his sons, immortal and ruling with him. And not just them, Satan too.

“Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height”, “I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen”. Historically it is talking about Babylon, but since he is comparing him to Adam, the mighty one is Satan. “I have driven him out for his wickedness.”

“Upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken”. Before, his branches were not like the other trees; now his branches are fallen. His boughs and branches are in paradise. “And all the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow, and have left him”: now it is talking about the earth. All the children he had on the earth that he was ruling over are no longer under his rule. This is how Adam’s kingdom fell.

Everything here is before Adam fell. It is not talking about Seth, or Cain and Abel. This is him being kicked out. He had kids, nations and kings before he was kicked out.

“To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height”: those trees are us, the twelve tribes of Israel in the heavens. We couldn’t exalt ourselves no more because our leader, our king, fell. “All that drink water”, all of us drinking those living waters from heaven: “for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth”.

That does not mean we just died.
