All Adam’s sons, all his boughs and branches, were delivered to the nether parts of the earth: now we have to come down through Adam, starting with Seth, be born and go through tribulations and overcome. “In the midst of the children of men”: they were not regular men; now they go down in the midst of the children of men, with them that die. That goes back to 2 Esdras 7: the entrance to this world is now narrow; back then it was wide.

“In the day when he went down to the grave”: the day Adam was cast out. “I covered the deep for him”: the deep is the sea, going into wisdom. “And I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed”. The water that was flowing, that his boughs and branches were drinking, God restrained: no water was coming to Adam no more. The great waters are the living waters of Revelation 22, and they stopped when Adam fell.

“I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him”: Lebanon and the trees are his children. We fainted for him.

“I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell”. The hell there is the grave, sheol: the earth. Adam was cast down to the earth. And what did the Lord do because of that? He withdrew paradise. He pulled paradise up off the earth. Paradise was a spiritual realm connected to the earth, and when it was pulled away it caused devastation: millions and millions of the children Adam had on the earth died, like the flood. A few were left, and that is where Cain found his wife.

“And all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water”: the apostles, the 144, all Christ’s top leaders, all Adam’s leaders that were with him, “shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.”

precepts.why: To explain his branches. “In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.” The branches of the Lord are Israel: those of us that escape that destruction and get the kingdom. We are those branches that are beautiful.

What are his boughs that were multiplied? “Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”, “Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us.”

“Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it.” “The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.” The boughs are Israel: the sons of God.

To explain his height exalted above all the trees. “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs. And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest”. The Lord is comparing Egypt to Adam: not just Adam, but Adam’s kingdom, Adam ruling. What we read in Genesis 2, we get more insight into here.
“And let all the angels of God worship him.” The fowls of heaven that made their nests in his boughs are the angels. All the angels were under Adam when he was ruling.
Who are the beasts of the field? “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field”. Satan was there, among the beasts of the field, and he was under Adam.

This explains that all nations were under him. “And immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Out of number means you could not number them, so many that he was living for a long time, before he was kicked out and lost his immortality.

“I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it”: this is talking about Christ. “In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing”: the same as Ezekiel 31. He is going to plant it in the height of Israel, where it was before.

“I the Lord have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish”: he brought them down, and he brings them back up again.

The nations that were born to Adam on the earth, in the flesh. “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”. All the children Adam had on the earth before the fall were born in vain, because his true children were his firstborn in the heavens, ruling with him.

To understand the kingdom of Adam, you have to understand the kingdom that is to come. Once you understand how the Lord is going to set up the kingdom in the future, it is the same thing: us ruling with Christ in righteousness, and nobody able to hurt us.

“The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee”. The heathen are going to envy us when Christ returns and sets us back on this earth to rule. It was the same back then: they envied us and couldn’t do nothing. It is going to be the same when Christ returns: they will envy us, but they will not be able to do anything against us. We will be immortal.

“For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” The man he created was Adam. Adam was immortal and his sons were immortal; the children he had on the earth before he fell were not immortal. They were not created in his image; they were sons of men.

“Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world”. The devil also envied Adam. Satan went to war with Adam; he couldn’t get him, so he went through his woman to take him down: he jumped on his wife, played with her emotions and tricked her. That is how death came.
“So he drove out the man”. Adam was driven out because he sinned. He was kicked out of paradise, down to the earth, and had no more access to go up there.

“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” This was so in the beginning, and it is going to be the same way in the future.

“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness”. Today we walk in darkness. We don’t know and don’t understand that we are gods: the beings that were with Adam in the beginning, ruling and judging this earth, with him before the earth was created. We don’t understand the power that we have.

“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That is the branches and the boughs. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” Why does it say that? Because it was not like that in the beginning. After Adam fell, that is what happened.

“We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have an eternal body in the heavens: the same body we had with Adam in the beginning.

After Adam sinned, the Lord appointed that all of us have to come on the earth through Adam, in the flesh, and fight to get the kingdom, the same way Christ came, overcame and walked right. It is not going to be given unto us no more. In the beginning it was wide and sure: once Christ created you as one of the tribes, you got the kingdom. Because Adam fell, we all have to be born into the nether parts of the earth and work for the kingdom. You need to understand who you are.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All the creatures are waiting for the sons of God to be manifest. In Genesis it calls us the sons of God, and the sons of God are the twelve tribes of Israel.

“The creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption”: we want to be delivered from this corrupted body. “Even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want back the body we had in the beginning, before Adam fell.

To some this is foolishness; to others it is the power of God. You have to see what the Bible says: that is faith.

“It had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam”: the earth was given to Adam to rule, and he ruled the heaven and the earth. “Or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning”: Ezra is telling the Lord, why didn’t you stop Adam from sinning? Why give him the earth when you knew he was going to sin?

“For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness, and after death to look for punishment?” We have to come on this earth and live in heaviness, the nations whooping our behind, and after we die we are going to be punished again.

“O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Adam did not fall by himself; he was not the only one kicked out of paradise. All his children fell with him. That is why Christ came and died for our sins: through one man sin came into the world, and through one man life comes into the world. He messed up and said, I am going to fix it. Christ came and fixed it: Adam came back and fixed it, walked perfect and died for our sins. So Christ is going to choose which of us go back with him to paradise and rule the heaven and the earth: you are real, you asked for forgiveness, you messed up but you never gave up.

“Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?” Christ descended first. Him being born on the earth is called descending. The lower parts of the earth are here in captivity: the nether parts of the earth where his sons were cast out to. How did they descend? They had to be born into the earth.

“But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.” The mother of us all means we all came from there. That is why Christ says, I am not of this world, and tells us, you are not of this world; love not the world. That is why the Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers on this earth, and why, if they had been mindful of whence they came, they might have had opportunity to return. There are different levels of understanding to these scriptures.

Two of our forefathers, created in the image of God: the sons of God coming down on the earth, cast down to the nether parts of the earth. All our forefathers’ names have a meaning behind them, going into what took place back then.

“And Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch”. Jared means descend, descent. Where did he descend from? It goes back to Ezekiel 31: they were cast down to the nether parts of the earth. He came down here and died, just like Adam: Adam did not die when he sinned, but eventually died of old age. Death was pronounced on all the sons in the heaven: they did not die up there in their spiritual bodies; they have to come and be born on the earth and go through their trials.

“And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.” Enoch walked perfect and went back to paradise. Enoch means dedicated, trained. Enoch came down on the earth, trained himself to conquer the flesh, became perfect, and God took him back up to paradise.

This explains how he caused the nations to shake. “And immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments. And again in process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them. And it came to pass in every of them, that as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.”

As death was to Adam, so was the flood to these: when Adam fell and the nations shook, there was a great destruction on the earth. The Lord killed millions and millions of people when Adam fell, when paradise was withdrawn from the earth. Just like the flood, a few were left over, and that is where Cain found his wife.

How are we comforted in the nether parts of the earth? “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The scriptures comfort us. After we were cast down, the Lord sent prophets to teach us the scriptures and give us hope, to try to get back the kingdom. All his sons have to come on the earth and go through their trials and tribulations in the flesh.

sense.text: “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. What we just read is basically Adam’s kingdom. What comes next is in time.
“So God created man in his own image”: Adam was created in the image of God, to be immortal and righteous after God’s eternity. “Male and female created he them.”

“And God blessed them”: he blessed Adam and Eve. Even though they messed up, they were still blessed; God forgave them.

“Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth”. Why does the earth need to be replenished? Because after Adam’s sin there was a great destruction on the earth. And not just to replenish the earth, but to replenish it with children in his image and after his likeness.

“And subdue it.” The earth was given to Adam; why does he need to subdue it? Because he lost it. Who has rulership of the earth now? Satan said all the power and glory of this earth was given to him, and he can give it to whom he will. Adam lost rulership of this earth, so now he has to come and subdue the earth and kill Satan. The earth has not been subdued by Adam as yet; that is for another time.

precepts.why:
“And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” A man: Cain was not created in Adam’s image. We keep reading about the children of men, and his very name lets you know he was not in Adam’s image or after his likeness.

“And she again bare his brother Abel.” Abel was righteous and Cain was wicked. Abel was supposed to be that righteous child created in Adam’s image, but Cain killed him. Genesis 4 and 5 is the earth being replenished.

“This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam”. Adam means from the ground: that is where they came from.

“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image”. This is when the sons of God above start being sent down on the earth, cast down to the nether parts of the earth and born through Adam and his descendants: the twelve tribes up there being born into the earth, in the image and likeness of God. Cain was not born in the image of God. The whole lineage of Seth is the sons of God: Israel being born into the earth.

Genesis 2 is Adam’s rulership; Genesis 2 and 3 is Ezekiel 31, Adam’s rule and Adam’s fall; Genesis 4 and 5 is Adam and Eve replenishing the earth with the righteous seed after Adam’s fall.
